type.name: ConjunctiveOperator
type.description: These operators are case-sensitive. Conjunctive operators in the same array must match for a query to work. To mix operators use nested queries with query pairs containing a query_list. The following are the available conjunctive operators:

values.name: AND_NEXT
values.description: The results of the query have to meet all the conditions in the query pair list.

values.name: NONE_NEXT
values.description: The final query pair in the list should use this operator since it has nothing to connect to.

values.name: OR_NEXT
values.description: The results of the query have to meet one of the conditions in the query pair list.

values.name: EQUAL
values.description: The data is equal to the value.

values.name: GREATER_EQUAL
values.description: The data is greater than or equal to the value.

values.name: GREATER_THAN
values.description: The data is greater than the value.

values.name: IN_LIST
values.description: The data is in the list of values.

values.name: LESS_EQUAL
values.description: The data is less than or equal to the value.

values.name: LESS_THAN
values.description: The data is less than the value.

values.name: LIKE
values.description: The data is like the value. The value can contain wildcard characters.

values.name: NOT_EQUAL
values.description: The data is not equal to the value.

values.name: NOT_IN_LIST
values.description: The data is not in the list of values.

values.name: NOT_LIKE
values.description: The data is not like the value. The value can contain wildcard characters.

fields.name: query_group
fields.description: A list of query pairs to use to build out a nested query. A more detailed example is below under the examples section.

fields.name: value
